cases.prompt: We just want to start fuzzing our C JSON library. Should we use LibAFL?

any.why: points to a standard fuzzer for a quick start

expectations: Recommends starting with libFuzzer (or AFL++ for multi-core) because the target is a standard C library and LibAFL adds complexity.
Names when LibAFL is the right choice: custom mutators or feedback, unsupported targets or architectures, or research.
Mentions that LibAFL can later act as a libFuzzer drop-in using the same harness.

cases.prompt: We need a custom mutator for our bytecode VM, so we are building a LibAFL fuzzer. Outline its parts.
expectations: Lists the components: observers, feedback, objective (crashes or timeouts), state with corpus, mutators, scheduler and executor.
Places the custom bytecode mutator in the mutator stage.
Mentions building the target through a LibAFL compiler wrapper (libafl_cc) to get coverage instrumentation.
